raw_response:
I farm only 6 mu, so I keep the plan tight and labor-efficient. Because I have 50 years of experience, high education, and reliable well irrigation, I will run an intensive but controlled system instead of spreading myself too thin. I will keep the main rotation on the core land as cabbage, then maize, then spinach, because that matches my usual system and helps me use land across seasons. I will also keep some area in chili and kidney bean for cash flow and diversification. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly gives me stronger uniformity, yield, and marketability. I will fertilize cabbage and spinach more heavily because they respond well and I want stable vegetable yields, while kidney bean gets lighter nitrogen because too much nitrogen pushes vine growth over pod set. Maize will get moderate fertilizer and a few irrigations tied to key growth stages. I will mostly use rotary tillage because my farm is small, I have irrigation, and rotary tillage is efficient for quick seasonal turnover. I will keep pesticide use moderate, not excessive, because I want to control risk without wasting money. My goal is steady output, manageable labor for a two-person household, and good use of the full year.
